acceptance_limits: Two independent guest kernels are a proposed functional environment, not infrastructure fault-domain independence.

http_head_only.limitation: Detached signature filename was not confirmed; whether SHA512SUMS is clearsigned has not been read.

http_head_only.selection: Official source tarball exists, but building QEMU is not the recommended bounded method.

missing_premises: Principal must record the proposed functional same-physical-host profile and limits before any setup is authorised.
No actual QEMU binary/libslirp/firmware or boot execution has been tested; signed package dependency closure and extracted size remain unknown and must fit the owned budget.
The image signature/checksum format and immutable build/version must be verified before downloading/booting; HEAD requests alone do not authenticate image bytes.
SMBIOS NoCloud bootstrap and restricted user-network HTTP forwards require an actual bounded probe; no peer reachability is currently proven.
Current memory headroom and storage must be re-read immediately before each guest. There is no reserved budget; page-cache reclaim must not be assumed as a guarantee.

Cached Python images are3.12.15, while current project host runtime is3.12.14. Neither host-venv copying nor compatible application/runtime/state/package transfer is proven; full native delivery is separate from this small boot probe.
not_performed: No artifact body downloads; only HTTP HEAD requests.
No VM/container start, rootfs extraction, overlay creation, daemon/service/network configuration changes.
No source/docs edits, branch operations, commits or venv sync.
No old-soak or owned PG17 access or cleanup.

apt_simulation.result: No package indexes for QEMU candidates; protected80-applied-apt-retries config was unreadable. No update/install/download was run.

profile_state: proposed local-qemu-tcg-v1, pending Principal discussion record; no QEMU appendix was present in ADR-0047 at inspection.

proposed_hard_budgets.measurement: Count allocated st_blocks bytes for unique owned inodes, not virtual qcow2/apparent sizes. Because/tmp is tmpfs, budget those bytes as memory too. Stop only owned VMs on a guard violation; do not prune/drop caches or touch another campaign.

previously_discussed_ceiling_per_guest.note: Ceiling only, not demonstrated capacity; do not start at this memory size under present pressure.

recommended_staged_method: After explicit root/architect go-ahead, create one owned0700 run directory under/tmp/ariadne-local-qemu-tcg-v1/<run-id>; leave the repository/workspace/venv and all existing Docker/PG resources untouched.

Use native/usr/bin/apt-get with an owned APT_CONFIG/state/cache/source-list prefix, skip protected system config parts, verify Debian InRelease/Packages using the installed Debian archive keyring, and fetch pinned qemu-system-x86/qemu-system-common/qemu-system-data/qemu-utils/firmware plus only required missing libraries. Extract .deb files with dpkg-deb into the owned toolchain; do not invoke dpkg installation or host service changes.

Verify the exact image checksum/signature format, pin image+tool package digests, and retain one immutable Debian cloud qcow2 base. Use separate sparse COW overlays, no9p/virtiofs/shared writable guest filesystem.

Boot the first guest with TCG,1vCPU/1GiB, headless serial log, private QMP socket and own overlay. Use SMBIOS NoCloud HTTP seed to avoid ISO-tool installation if supported by the official image; verify support by the bounded probe. Only after the first guest is healthy and resource guards pass, boot the second.

Use QEMU user networking/libslirp with restrict mode and explicitly configured loopback-only host forwards/guest forwards for owned HTTP endpoints. No TAP/TUN/KVM, SSH route, VPN, external guest egress or proxy bypass is required. Exact guestfwd semantics remain to be verified once binaries are available.

Guest bootstrap, package/state/object examples move via explicit HTTP and content hashes. Do not mount the host source tree, object directory or socket into either guest. Distinct guest boot IDs/machine IDs must be observed from each live kernel, not inferred from labels or runner IDs.

The owned controller retains exact QEMU PID/startticks+pidfd and only declares provider stop after kill and actual wait/reap. A timeout/network loss is never a stop witness. This boot/HTTP/whole-VM-stop probe remains infrastructure evidence only.
scope: Read-only infrastructure discovery only; not NI2-053 implementation or A47-04 acceptance.
